title: Efficiency Bounds for the ATT under the Union of Parallel Trends and Synthetic Control
banked_reason: The note proves branch influence-function classes, their intersection-based convolution lower bound, finite Gram criteria, and an explicit strict-gap witness, but it does not prove that any estimator attains the union bound.
gap_reasons: it does not prove that any estimator attains the union bound
the advertised oracle-adaptation frontier characterizes equality of abstract variance bounds rather than existence of a procedure that adapts to either branch at those bounds
they supply neither implementable inference nor evidence that the diagnostic improves either cited application
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived the strict-interior, locally constant-rank PT/SC influence classes, corrected their common treated-composition term, computed the union lower bound by finite covariance-weighted QPs, and proved exact oracle-equality criteria, endpoint reductions, and a strict three-group witness. The requested uniform attaining estimator collapsed: finite-coordinate splicing rules out the frozen sequence-class claim, while a positive result on a conventional common neighborhood would require a new package proving profiled-normal estimation, uniform rank stability, asymptotic linearity, variance consistency, and multiplier validity. Both final correctness referees passed with no findings, but the delivered characterization-only package remained incremental.
tldr: Short-panel ATT identification is valid on the union of conditional parallel trends and a full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction. At strict-interior, locally constant-rank intersection points, the corrected derivative separates the common treated-composition gradient \(\chi_0\) from conditionally centered stratum gradients. Their affine-class intersection and union convolution lower bound are computed by finite covariance-weighted programs, with \(E[\chi_0^2]\) added to the envelope and both oracle variances; observable Gram discrepancies characterize simultaneous and one-sided adaptation. The exact strict three-group witness and the single-donor and saturated-donor endpoints remain valid on this repaired scope. Sun, Xie, and Zhang analyze one integrated ATT estimator and one multiplier-bootstrap construction under alternative PT and SC hypotheses, with branch-specific influence functions and variances. This paper adds a sharp local lower-bound benchmark, not implemented inference; finite-coordinate splicing makes the requested uniform attainment theorem false over the frozen sequence class.
gap: SunXieZhang2025 identifies the ATT under PT or SC but proves distinct branchwise influence and bootstrap results; ChenSantAnnaXie2025 derives the PT efficiency bound alone. Neither source determines the regular influence class or convolution lower bound for the nonconvex union at an intersection law.
fill: The project derives the profiled branch normal spans, solves their affine intersection by stratum quadratic programs, expresses oracle adaptation as zero-valued Gram discrepancies, supplies a strict three-group region, and defines the active-chart score needed to pose uniform branch-switching inference without evaluating an intersection-only gradient off the intersection.
